recipes.name: 4:6 method (Tetsu Kasuya)
recipes.notes: Five equal pours of 60 g. The first two decide sweetness and acidity: pour the first 40 percent in two goes and the balance shifts (a smaller first pour is sweeter, a larger one brighter). The last three decide strength: more pours, stronger coffee. Wait for the water to drain a little between pours. Medium-coarse grind. Patterns are a suggestion.

recipes.name: Ultimate V60 (James Hoffmann)
recipes.notes: Bloom with twice to three times the coffee weight and stir so every grain is wet, pour to 60 percent, then to the full amount, then a gentle swirl to flatten the bed. A medium-fine grind and water just off the boil. Aim for a drawdown that is done around 3:30.

recipes.name: Single pour V60 (Scott Rao)
recipes.notes: A bloom of about 50 g with a stir, then one slow, steady pour in a spiral, keeping the water level constant. A gentle stir and a spin at the end flatten the bed so the drawdown is even.

recipes.name: Inverted AeroPress
recipes.notes: Inverted: put the plunger in a little to seal it, add the coffee and all the water, stir, steep, then flip onto your cup and press slowly for about 30 seconds.

recipes.name: French press, 4 minutes
recipes.notes: Pour all the water over the coffee in circles, put the lid on without pressing, and wait. At four minutes break the crust with a spoon, skim off the foam, wait a few more minutes for the grounds to settle and press gently, or just pour. Coarse grind.
